analysis.investment_thesis: HEG is a highly cyclical graphite electrode manufacturer trading at 3.5× its Graham Number (~INR 180), with a P/E of 32 on severely depressed earnings of only INR 115 Cr. The business has recorded losses in 2017 and 2021, and current ROE of 2.59% is an insult to any patient capital.
key_strengths: Low leverage: Debt/Equity of 0.14, well within Graham's 0.5 limit
Interest coverage of ~6.5× (Operating Income 255 Cr ÷ Finance Cost 39 Cr) — adequate safety
Large asset base: Total Equity of INR 4,666 Cr provides some liquidation cushion
key_risks: Extreme cyclicality: Net profit swung from INR 3,026 Cr (2019) to -18 Cr (2021) to 115 Cr (2025) — no stable earning power
Price far above Graham Number: sqrt(22.5 × EPS ~5.96 × BVPS ~242) ≈ INR 180 vs. market price of INR 633
Structural earnings deterioration: operating income collapsed from INR 4,662 Cr (2019) to INR 255 Cr (2025), with no visible recovery catalyst
red_flags: P/E of 32 — more than double Graham's maximum of 15, on already depressed earnings
P/B of 2.62 — nearly double Graham's ceiling of 1.5; no margin of safety in asset value
Losses in two of last nine years (2017, 2021) — violates the 3–5 consecutive years of positive earnings requirement
ROE of only 2.59% — management is earning less than a fixed deposit on shareholders' capital
Other income (INR 145 Cr) constitutes over half of operating income (INR 255 Cr), masking operating weakness
analysis.detailed_analysis:
HEG Limited fails every primary quantitative test I impose. At INR 633, the Graham Number — the geometric mean anchored to current EPS (~INR 5.96) and book value per share (~INR 242) — yields roughly INR 180, meaning the stock must fall 72% before I would even begin to consider it. The P/E of 32 is built on earnings that themselves look artificially depressed after the 2018–2019 graphite electrode supercycle ended. Mr. Market is pricing in a recovery that may never arrive at the same magnitude, and he is asking me to pay for that hope — a fool's bargain.

The business is a commodity cyclical at its core: graphite electrode pricing is dictated by global EAF steel output and Chinese production, not by any durable competitive advantage HEG possesses. The profit history — INR 1,099 Cr profit in 2018, then losses in 2021, then recovery, then renewed decline to INR 115 Cr in 2025 — is precisely the kind of volatile, unpredictable earnings stream I refuse to capitalize at any premium. The intelligent investor seeks a business whose value can be estimated with confidence; HEG offers no such assurance. I will wait patiently for Mr. Market to offer this at or below book value with sustained positive earnings — conditions that do not exist today.
